key_insight: ArcTN finds lower-cost tensor-network contraction orders while reducing planning time, improving the efficiency of classical quantum-circuit simulation.
engineering_relevance: Light and Heavy search presets trade planning effort for refinement, while tensor slicing helps satisfy intermediate-tensor size limits.
method: Combine randomized-greedy construction, subtree reconfiguration, and parallel tempering.
Use stage-specific stopping rules in Light and Heavy search presets.
Apply Fixed or Dynamic slicing to meet tensor-size limits.
evidence_signal: On 30 QC32 networks completed by all eight configurations, Light used 61.32% fewer FLOPs and planned 1.62× faster than Cotengra Auto/CMA-ES; Heavy used 43.83% fewer FLOPs and planned 7.21× faster than AutoHQ/Optuna.
watch_item: Dynamic slicing requires longer planning, and results restricted to runs completed by all compared configurations may not generalize to every circuit workload.
paper_title: ArcTN: Efficient Tensor-Network Contraction Planning for Quantum Circuit Simulation
